question:
Deployment `freight-api` in namespace `freight` must run with its own read-only identity.

- Create ServiceAccount `freight-reader`, a Role `freight-reader` and a RoleBinding `freight-reader` that grant it `get`, `list` and `watch` on ConfigMaps and `get` on the Secret `route-key` only. In namespace `freight` the ServiceAccount must end up with no permissions beyond these; do not change what any other subject is allowed to do.
- Make `freight-api` run as `freight-reader`, with the ServiceAccount token mounted into its Pods.
- Write the output of these three commands, in this order, one per line, to `/home/candidate/exam/q6/can-i.txt`:
  - `kubectl auth can-i watch configmaps -n freight --as=system:serviceaccount:freight:freight-reader`
  - `kubectl auth can-i get secret/route-key -n freight --as=system:serviceaccount:freight:freight-reader`
  - `kubectl auth can-i get secret/tariff-db -n freight --as=system:serviceaccount:freight:freight-reader`

Verify with: `kubectl auth can-i --list -n freight --as=system:serviceaccount:freight:freight-reader`

verification.description: ServiceAccount, Role and RoleBinding freight-reader exist and are bound together
freight-reader can get/list/watch ConfigMaps and get only Secret route-key, nothing more
Pre-existing edit grant no longer reaches freight-reader; yardmaster and freight-writer keep their access
freight-api Pods run as freight-reader with the API token mounted
